title: Duplicate WIZNET5K driver/library files in MicroPython tree
body: I noticed that the WIZNET5K files are duplicated in the tree. The copy in lib/wiznet5k appears to be the latest and linked to the WIZNET development branch, while drivers/wiznet5k contains a similar but very old set taken from the W5500_EVB ioLibrary in August 2014. Should the older files be removed and dependent builds changed to use the newer copy? Apparently only the stm32 port relies on the old version. I can modify its Makefile and network_wiznet5k.c references, but I have no STM32 platform on which to test.

symptoms_visible: I can see two similar WIZNET5K source trees: a newer copy under lib/wiznet5k and an old 2014 copy under drivers/wiznet5k.
The stm32 port still appears to reference the old copy.
N0.label: N0 duplicate WIZNET5K sources reported

symptoms_visible: My initial default PYBV11 build succeeded, but it had not enabled the WIZNET5K driver.
When the WIZNET5K sources are actually enabled, simply changing the directory references exposes compile and link errors.
N1.label: N1 real WIZNET build requirements established

symptoms_visible: After removing the old WIZNET5K sources, switching the Makefile to lib/wiznet5k and extmod/network_wiznet5k.c, and adding the SPI type alias, my clean PYBV11 builds complete for both W5200 and W5500 when lwIP is not enabled.
N2_x.label: N2_x partial migration compiles without lwIP

symptoms_visible: On a PYBV11 with a W5500 breakout, nic.active(True) raises OSError: 16 and prints 'MPY: enabling IRQs'.
With lwIP enabled, extmod/network_wiznet5k.c does not compile because mp_hal_pin_interrupt and the pin-trigger constants are undeclared.
N3.label: N3 partial migration fails hardware and lwIP tests

symptoms_visible: The updated candidate branch builds with the STM32-specific SPI and interrupt adaptations included.
N4.label: N4 complete STM32 integration candidate

symptoms_visible: On my PYBV11 with a W5500 breakout, the candidate can activate the interface and communicate instead of raising OSError: 16.
The lwIP interrupt configuration also runs, and at 20 MHz SPI I see about 0.75 ms external ping time and 1.3 ms from the board.
N5.label: N5 candidate verified on STM32 hardware

symptoms_visible: The tree uses the shared lib/wiznet5k and extmod driver instead of the duplicate old STM32 copy, and W5500 networking works on PYBV11 with the required STM32 adaptations.
N_terminal.label: terminal duplicate driver removed and STM32 integration working

question_patterns: What exact make command did you use when the STM32 build succeeded?
Was the WIZNET5K network option explicitly enabled in that build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My first successful PYBV11 build was just the default build, so it was not compiling the WIZNET5K path. I then found the MICROPY_PY_NETWORK_WIZNET5K option and rebuilt with it enabled.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Yes, my original clean build already used MICROPY_PY_NETWORK_WIZNET5K=5500 and exercised the replacement sources without any errors.
I first tested PYBV10 rather than PYBV11, but the original build still omitted the WIZNET5K option.

question_patterns: Can you rebuild PYBV11 with the WIZNET5K option enabled and report the raw result?
Please run a clean WIZNET-enabled build rather than the default STM32 build.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I rebuilt with `make BOARD=PYBV11 MICROPY_PY_NETWORK_WIZNET5K=5500`. The new library has paths such as `Ethernet/W5500/w5500.c`, and after switching to extmod/network_wiznet5k.c I reached a remaining `machine_spi_type` link error.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The clean WIZNET-enabled build succeeds unchanged while still using drivers/wiznet5k and stm32/modnwwiznet5k.c.

question_patterns: Are the source paths and APIs identical between the old and new WIZNET trees?
What changes are needed beyond replacing the directory name?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. The newer tree uses different path capitalization, such as `Ethernet/W5500`, and the STM32-specific module cannot simply be compiled against it unchanged.

edges.comment: The initial successful build was misleading because the driver was disabled. The enabled build exposed source-layout and integration differences. The affected PYBV11 hardware tester is folded into the simulated user side.

solution.intent: Perform a direct source-tree migration: remove the old WIZNET5K and STM32-specific driver files, point the STM32 Makefile at lib/wiznet5k and extmod/network_wiznet5k.c, correct source-path capitalization, and alias machine_spi_type to machine_hard_spi_type.
solution.concrete_example: Remove drivers/wiznet5k, stm32/modnwwiznet5k.c and stm32/network_wiznet5k.c; compile extmod/network_wiznet5k.c and the selected lib/wiznet5k Ethernet sources; add `#define machine_spi_type machine_hard_spi_type` so the build links.
solution.inference_hint: This direct migration is only compile-complete. Hardware and lwIP testing later show that the alias and Makefile changes do not provide the runtime SPI-object and pin-interrupt adaptations required by the shared extmod driver.

edges.comment: This was actually implemented and cleanly built for W5200 and W5500 without lwIP, but it was incomplete: W5500 activation failed on hardware and the lwIP configuration did not compile.

question_patterns: Can you flash the candidate onto a PYBV11 with a W5500 and try activating the interface?
What happens on real STM32 hardware when you call nic.active(True)?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested the no-lwIP build on a PYBV11 with a W5500 breakout. Calling `nic.active(True)` gives `OSError: 16`, followed by `MPY: enabling IRQs`. Attempts to communicate with the W5500 fail.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The interface activates and communicates normally on the W5500; I cannot reproduce OSError: 16.
I get the same OSError: 16 using a different SPI bus and different chip-select pin.

question_patterns: Can you also build the migrated driver with lwIP enabled and paste the compiler errors?
Does the shared WIZNET driver compile in its interrupt-based lwIP configuration on STM32?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With lwIP enabled, compilation stops in extmod/network_wiznet5k.c. It says `mp_hal_pin_interrupt` is implicitly declared and that `MP_HAL_PIN_TRIGGER_FALL` and `MP_HAL_PIN_TRIGGER_NONE` are undeclared.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The lwIP configuration builds and its interrupt callback runs correctly without any STM32 pin-HAL changes.

edges.comment: These are handler-initiated build and hardware measurements. The raw OSError and compiler output are user-side evidence; the SPI double-unwrapping diagnosis belongs to the consuming solution.

solution.intent: Complete the STM32 migration by adapting the SPI object passed to the shared WIZNET driver and adding the STM32 pin-interrupt definitions needed by its lwIP mode, while retaining the consolidation on lib/wiznet5k and extmod/network_wiznet5k.c.
solution.concrete_example: Keep the consolidated lib/extmod driver, but correct the STM32 SPI conversion so the transfer routine receives the object level it expects rather than dereferencing an already-unwrapped SPI pointer. Add the STM32 pin-interrupt operation and trigger definitions required by the shared driver's interrupt-enabled lwIP path.
solution.inference_hint: The hardware output only reports failed W5500 communication and OSError: 16. Tracing STM32's spi_from_mp_obj return value through wiz_spi_write and machine_hard_spi_transfer to identify a second dereference is engineer-side inference.

edges.comment: The tester traced the runtime failure to the wrong SPI object level and extended the branch with STM32 pin-interrupt support for lwIP. This produces the complete pre-landing candidate.

question_patterns: Please flash the updated candidate on the PYBV11 with the W5500 and report whether activation and network traffic now work.
Can you retest the same W5500 startup script on the patched branch?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested it on my PYBV11 with the W5500 breakout. The interface activates and communicates now; the previous OSError: 16 no longer occurs. I used `machine.SPI(1, baudrate=20_000_000)` with the WIZNET5K constructor and configured the interface successfully.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The updated candidate still raises OSError: 16 as soon as I call nic.active(1).

question_patterns: Does the updated candidate also work with lwIP and the interrupt pin enabled?
Please test the interrupt-enabled network configuration and report the observed traffic or ping result.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The interrupt-enabled configuration works. After increasing SPI to 20 MHz, I measured about 0.75 ms ping time from outside and 1.3 ms from the board.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The no-lwIP mode works, but the lwIP build still fails on the missing pin-interrupt symbols.

edges.comment: Pre-landing verification on real PYBV11 and W5500 hardware, contributed by the second participant and folded into the simulated user side.

solution.intent: Land the verified consolidation: remove the obsolete duplicate WIZNET5K driver and STM32-specific implementation, use the maintained lib/wiznet5k plus shared extmod driver, and include the STM32 SPI and interrupt compatibility changes proven on W5500 hardware.
solution.concrete_example: Adopt the verified changes that remove drivers/wiznet5k and the old STM32 WIZNET module, update the STM32 build to use lib/wiznet5k and extmod/network_wiznet5k.c, and retain the SPI-object and pin-interrupt adaptations required for working W5500 and lwIP operation.
solution.inference_hint: The accepted resolution is not merely deleting duplicate files. The migration exposed two STM32 integration defects: the shared driver received the wrong SPI object level, preventing transfers, and its lwIP path required pin-interrupt HAL support absent from STM32. Both compatibility changes were included and tested before the issue was declared handled.

edges.comment: The reporter subsequently stated that the issue had been taken care of by the submitted change. Coordination and merge bookkeeping are not separately scored.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted resolution as consolidating STM32 on the maintained lib/wiznet5k sources and shared extmod/network_wiznet5k.c implementation, allowing the obsolete duplicate driver and STM32-specific WIZNET files to be removed.

Must explain that a directory replacement and machine_spi_type alias were insufficient: on STM32 the migrated driver passed the wrong SPI object level, so no SPI transfer occurred and W5500 activation raised OSError: 16.
Must account for the separate lwIP integration requirement: STM32 needed the pin-interrupt function and trigger definitions expected by the shared WIZNET driver.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the explicitly enabled WIZNET build, the W5500 hardware activation result, and the lwIP compiler output rather than the successful default or no-lwIP compilation alone.
Must not present the initial compile-only migration as the complete fix; it was falsified by hardware and lwIP testing.
Must have the consolidated candidate verified on real STM32/W5500 hardware, including the interrupt-enabled path, before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced source-level contributor who can edit Makefiles and C headers, perform clean cross-builds with feature flags, inspect linker errors, and share firmware, but lacks STM32 hardware; a second contributor with a PYBV11 and W5500 supplies hardware testing and low-level diagnosis, folded into one simulated user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Collaborative and iterative; posts exact commands, source blocks, build output, and incremental findings; readily acknowledges missed build options and coordinates testing with the hardware-owning contributor.
